comparisons.peer_topic: THATIC JV Entity List Designation and Compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: In June 2019, THATIC and the THATIC JV were added to the U.S. Department of Commerce's Entity List, and the Company is complying with applicable U.S. laws regarding this designation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose legal compliance matters in Item 8, but the nature and subject differ. Intel's disclosure focuses on active securities litigation alleging misleading statements regarding its foundry business growth and segment reporting changes. In contrast, AMD's relevant disclosure concerns regulatory compliance with the U.S. Entity List designation for specific Chinese entities (THATIC), rather than securities litigation regarding financial disclosures or business operations.

sentences.text: A securities class action lawsuit was filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California in May 2024 against us and certain officers following the modification of our segment reporting in the first quarter of 2024 to align to our new internal foundry operating model.

In August 2024 the court ordered the case consolidated with a second, similar lawsuit, and in October 2024 plaintiffs filed an amended consolidated complaint generally alleging that defendants violated the federal securities laws by making false or misleading statements about the growth and prospects of the foundry business and seeking monetary damages on behalf of all persons and entities that purchased or otherwise acquired our common stock or purchased call options or sold put options on our common stock from January 25, 2024 through August 1, 2024.
In June 2019, the Bureau of Industry and Security of the United States Department of Commerce added certain Chinese entities to the Entity List, including THATIC and the THATIC JV.
The Company is complying with U.S. law pertaining to the Entity List designation.

comparisons.peer_topic: In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation Status
comparisons.peer_summary: The Ninth Circuit affirmed in part and reversed in part the dismissal of the securities class action on August 25, 2023; NVIDIA obtained a stay of the mandate on December 5, 2023, pending its petition for certiorari to the Supreme Court, with a filing deadline of March 4, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA (NVDA) are defending against securities class action lawsuits alleging violations of federal securities laws through false or misleading statements. Intel's litigation was filed in May 2024 following segment reporting changes and involves a motion to dismiss. NVIDIA's litigation, originating in 2018 regarding channel inventory and cryptocurrency demand, saw the Ninth Circuit reverse a dismissal in August 2023, keeping the case active. Both disclose the procedural status and the nature of the alleged misleading statements in Item 8.

sentences.text: A securities class action lawsuit was filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California in May 2024 against us and certain officers following the modification of our segment reporting in the first quarter of 2024 to align to our new internal foundry operating model.
We filed a motion to dismiss the amended consolidated complaint in December 2024.

The plaintiffs in the putative securities class action lawsuit, captioned 4:18-cv-07669-HSG, initially filed on December 21, 2018 in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California, and titled In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation, filed an amended complaint on May 13, 2020.

On August 25, 2023, a majority of a three-judge Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in part and reversed in part the district court's dismissal of the case, with a third judge dissenting on the basis that the district court did not err in dismissing the case.
